To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel kernel-based approach for the maximum likelihood estimation of DPPs in the continuous case and we provide a controlled estimate for the correlation kernel of DPPs.

we propose a novel algorithm to solve a finite-dimensional optimization problem, with strong connections to the nonparametric MLE of a continuous DPP, and provide a controlled estimate for its correlation kernel.

we propose and analyze a nonparametric maximum-likelihood estimator for DPPs with continuous correlation kernel, based on a finite-dimensional optimization problem, that can be solved using a fixed point iteration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of a nonparametric inference procedure for DPPs in the continuous case, based on kernel methods, which we believe is the first such result.
the following questions: How can we estimate a DPP with a continuous ground set? How can we estimate the kernel of the DDP? What is the connection between the two problems?
the following questions: (i) Can nonparametric inference be performed on continuous DPPs? (ii) Can we provide a statistical estimate of the correlation function of continuous DPP?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonparametric MLE for DPPs is a kernel-based algorithm that is both tractable and interpretable.
we propose a novel kernel-based approach for the nonparametric inference for the correlation kernel of a DPP.
we have developed a new nonparametric method for estimating DPPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose the first nonparametric method for estimating the correlation kernel of a DPP.
we propose a novel nonparametric method to estimate the correlation kernel of a continuous DPP.
we provide the first nonparametric maximum-likelihood estimation method for DPPs in the continuous setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nonparametric estimation of a DPP is possible, even though the MLE problem is infinite dimensional.
kernel methods can be used to estimate DPPs in a nonparametric fashion.
nonparametric estimation of DPPs with a continuous ground set can be achieved with a finite-dimensional problem.
